item.title: Drought leaves Kapao families eating once a day
item.description: Families in Kapao in Menyama District are eating just one meal a day, drinking dirty creek water and struggling to send their children to school as a prolonged drought destroys food gardens and dries up water sources across 11 wards. item.content:encoded:
Families in Kapao in Menyama District are eating just one meal a day, drinking dirty creek water and struggling to send their children to school as a prolonged drought destroys food gardens and dries up water sources across 11 wards.

A drought assessment report prepared by Kapao LLG Drought Committee member Jackson Apa on October 2, 2026, warns that the situation could worsen without urgent government and humanitarian assistance.

“The situation remains critical and is expected to deteriorate without rapid interventions,” the report states.

The drought began in May, with little rainfall recorded across Kapao Local Level Government. The report says 11 of the 15 wards are affected, with Otete and Langimar facing the most serious conditions.

Community wells and water tanks have dried up, forcing villagers to walk two to four hours to collect water from creeks. The remaining water is described as muddy, contaminated and unsafe to drink without treatment.

The Kanakaimanga government station, four aid posts and seven primary schools have also run out of stored water.

Health facilities have recorded 36 cases of diarrhoea among children under five and 52 cases of water-related skin diseases. Of the skin disease cases, 34 were reported in Otete and 18 in Langimar. No drought-related deaths have been reported.

Food shortages are also worsening as gardens of kaukau, taro, bananas, cassava and vegetables have dried up. The report warns that little food is expected from gardens over the next three to four months.

The drought has also affected livestock, with reports of broiler chickens dying in Kamiakaka Ward because of a lack of water and feed. Pigs and dogs have also become malnourished and developed skin diseases.

Schools are facing growing challenges, with student attendance falling by 30 to 50 per cent across affected schools. Some children are missing classes because of illness and the need to collect water, while students and teachers are drinking untreated creek water.

The report warns that schools could be forced to close if water supplies run out completely.

Apa and the drought committee are calling for urgent food assistance, safe drinking water, medical supplies and water treatment tablets. They have also recommended emergency health and nutrition teams, school feeding programmes and long-term water projects, including boreholes and rainwater harvesting.

The report urges the Morobe Provincial Administration, Menyamya District authorities and humanitarian partners to support the response before conditions deteriorate further.

item.title: Fire destroys homes and church in SHP
item.description: A tragic fire fueled by strong winds has left a family in Southern Highlands province homeless and destitute after destroying several homes, a church, and properties estimated to worth over K200,000. The disastrous incident occurred at Lumbi village in the Imbonggu district.
item.content:encoded:
A tragic fire fueled by strong winds has left a family in Southern Highlands province homeless and destitute after destroying several homes, a church, and properties estimated to worth over K200,000.

The disastrous incident occurred at Lumbi village in the Imbonggu district.

According to local sources, the fire ignited when an elderly villager used fire to clear garden debris. A sudden surge of strong wind carried embers across to a nearby traditional kunai-thatched roof, quickly setting it ablaze and causing the fire to spread uncontrollably across the compound.

Speaking to NBC News, victim Job Pusa confirmed the catastrophic scale of the disaster. The fire completely destroyed his permanent house, six additional houses, and a Seventh-day Adventist (SDA) church building.

Beyond the loss of shelter, Mr. Pusa said a high-capacity generator that provided power services to the people, two chainsaws and specialized construction tools belonging to relatives employed with a local construction firm, all household belongings and domestic animals were all destroyed.

“The estimated cost of the properties and assets lost in the fire is around K200,000," Mr. Pusa stated, describing the heartbreak of seeing decades of hard work wiped out in minutes.

He stressed that the tragedy strikes at a time when the country is already struggling under the oppressive weight of an ongoing El Niño-induced drought. Local water sources in Lumbi village have completely dried up, and food gardens have failed, leaving people in a highly vulnerable state.

"While we were trying to cope with this dire situation, the fire struck and put us in an even more desperate position," Mr. Pusa said, describing his family as left completely homeless and helpless.

Mr. Pusa has issued an urgent plea to the Southern Highlands Provincial Disaster Committee and humanitarian organizations for swift relief assistance as they are facing immediate homelessness and a lack of basic supplies.

With water and food scarce due to the drought, the affected community members without prompt government intervention and emergency supplies, the displaced families face life-threatening hardship.

item.title: Indonesia bush fires linked to haze over Port Moresby
item.description: The National Weather Service [NWS] has confirmed that the haze currently affecting Port Moresby is linked to bush fires in Indonesia. NWS Deputy Director Kasis Inape has urged the public to take precautionary measures, including wearing face masks when outdoors and boiling drinking water before consumption.
item.content:encoded:
The National Weather Service [NWS] has confirmed that the haze currently affecting Port Moresby is linked to bush fires in Indonesia.

NWS Deputy Director Kasis Inape has urged the public to take precautionary measures, including wearing face masks when outdoors and boiling drinking water before consumption.

Haze has been visible over the city for the past two weeks, reducing visibility over long distances.

The haze occurs when tiny particles remain suspended in the air.

Mr Inape explains why the smoke and pollutants have remained in the atmosphere.

Mr Inape says the pollutants include carbon monoxide, which can harm people's health, particularly children and people with respiratory conditions.

With the hazy conditions continuing, the public is also being urged to avoid lighting unnecessary fires.

item.title: Police reservist graduates from secondary school
item.description: Thirty-four years, Enoch DelaCruz, a police reservist serving with the Esa’ala District Police in Milne Bay Province has achieved an uncommon milestone in the province by returning to the classroom and graduating on Saturday from Wesley Secondary School after being away from formal education for 16 years. ‎ ‎Having missed out on Grade 11 after completing Grade 10 in 2008, DelaCruz’s returned to sc
item.content:encoded:
Thirty-four years, Enoch DelaCruz, a police reservist serving with the Esa’ala District Police in Milne Bay Province has achieved an uncommon milestone in the province by returning to the classroom and graduating on Saturday from Wesley Secondary School after being away from formal education for 16 years. ‎ ‎Having missed out on Grade 11 after completing Grade 10 in 2008, DelaCruz’s returned to school for a second chance to fulfil his educational aspirations and pursue his dream of becoming a fully qualified police officer. ‎ ‎After completing Grade 10 at the then Wesley High School in 2008, DelaCruz did not progress to Grade 11. He remained at home until 2015 and joined the Esa’ala district Police as a reservist, dedicating himself to serving his community through law enforcement. For the next decade, he gained valuable experience in discipline, responsibility and community service. ‎ However, his ambition to become a fully qualified police officer remained unfulfilled. DelaCruz applied twice to attend Bomana Police College, but both attempts were unsuccessful. Rather than abandoning his dream, he decided to return to school and strengthen his qualifications. ‎ ‎In 2025, Wesley Secondary School Principal Davanai Robia gave him the opportunity to enrol in Grade 11 alongside other selected students from across Milne Bay province.

Returning to the classroom after years away presented a new challenge, particularly adapting to study alongside younger students. ‎ ‎"I attempted to speak with the school principal, Mr Robia, I verbally spoke to him once to return to school but he didn't believe in me. I didn't give up, I tried again the second time. He decided to give me a second chance. But actually, I had always had that motivation to strive and return to do Gr 11', DelaCruz said ‎ ‎ For him, obtaining a Grade 12 certificate was an important step towards realizing his ambition of gaining entry into Bomana Police College. ‎ ‎Coming from a policing background, he was appointed prefect responsible for justice and welfare, a role that allowed him to apply his experience in maintaining discipline and promoting the wellbeing of students. He embraced the responsibility, helping address disciplinary issues and supporting teachers in maintaining a safe and orderly learning environment. ‎ ‎ His commitment and leadership did not go unnoticed. ‎ DelaCruz has earned the admiration of the school’s principal and teachers for his outstanding contribution to student welfare, leadership and discipline. ‎ ‎Principal Robia described DelaCruz as one of the school's top students and commended his positive influence on the school community. ‎ ‎"One of our top students in academic and attitude. The change of environment at the school, Enoch was one of the most influential persons that helps teachers and the community to control the students. A very strong leader and transparent in his approach." principal Robia said. ‎ ‎DelaCruz’s achievement has also earned recognition from his colleagues in the Esa’ala District Police. Officer-in-Charge of Esa’ala District Police, Constable Ottio Herena, who attended the graduation, said DelaCruz, affectionately known as Rocky, was one of the force's dedicated officers.

‎Herena said the nickname reflected DelaCruz’s courage, commitment and willingness to take on challenging duties during police operations throughout the district. ‎ ‎"What he achieved has made us very proud as Esa’ala NCOs. We gave him a nickname 'Rocky' because he's one of the guys who shows a lot of interest in work and shows no fear. We call him Rocky when we are with him doing police operations around the district." ‎ ‎With his Grade 12 certificate now achieved, DelaCruz is looking ahead to the 2027 intake at Bomana Police College in Port Moresby. ‎ ‎His journey from police reservist to secondary school graduate demonstrates that setbacks do not have to define a person's future, and that determination can reopen doors once thought closed.

item.title: All Pacific clash tomorrow
item.description: Port Moresby’s Santos National Football Stadium is expected to be packed to capacity tomorrow for the all-Pacific double header of the 2026 Rugby League World Cup. The PNG Orchids are set to face the Fiji Bulikulas at 12.15pm followed by the blockbuster between the PNG Kumuls and Toa Samoa at 2.25pm.
item.content:encoded:
Port Moresby’s Santos National Football Stadium is expected to be packed to capacity tomorrow for the all-Pacific double header of the 2026 Rugby League World Cup.

The PNG Orchids are set to face the Fiji Bulikulas at 12.15pm followed by the blockbuster between the PNG Kumuls and Toa Samoa at 2.25pm.

PNG Rugby Football League General Manager for Performance and Pathways Tony Archer welcomed the visiting Fijian and Samoan teams yesterday at a welcome reception hosted by the Australian High Commission.

“We welcome you to Papua New Guinea,” Archer said in his speech at the Australian High Commission.

Australian High Commissioner to Papua New Guinea Ewen Macdonald also welcomed the visiting teams at the reception yesterday, and guaranteed Australia’s continuous support in developing rugby league throughout the Pacific region.

“I very much welcome you, it’s a privilege to have you here at the Australian High Commission,” he said.

“I also welcome you to PNG. It’s a great country and its s great place to play rugby league.”

“This weekend is special, its very special because it is an all-Pacific contest, showcasing Pacific talent and broadcasted live in a Pacific nation, Papua New Guinea, so it’s all Pacific.”

Meanwhile, NRL’s Senior Manager for Pacific Relations emphasized the broader significance rugby league delivers in PNG and the wider Pacific region.

“This weekend is just not about the results, it’s about national pride and cultural identity,” he said.

Tickets for the all- Pacific showdown tomorrow at the Santos National Football Stadium are all sold out.

item.title: Seventy-nine complete Gr 8 national exam at Sorovi primary
item.description: Sorovi Primary School, one of the top-performing primary schools in Oro Province, has successfully completed the 2026 National Grade 8 Examinations for its 79 students. Head Teacher Mrs. Yula Cimon confirmed this when addressing parents, students, and teachers during a small closing program held today to mark the end of the examination week.
item.content:encoded:
Sorovi Primary School, one of the top-performing primary schools in Oro Province, has successfully completed the 2026 National Grade 8 Examinations for its 79 students.

Head Teacher Mrs. Yula Cimon confirmed this when addressing parents, students, and teachers during a small closing program held today to mark the end of the examination week.

Mrs. Cimon said despite the challenges of El Niño and ‘Don’t Care’ activities affecting the province, the school successfully delivered both the Grade 8 National Examinations and the Grade 6 Benchmark Examinations simultaneously.

“God has protected the school, students and teachers to date, and the Grade 8 National Exams were conducted peacefully,” Mrs. Cimon said.

She extended her gratitude to the external and internal invigilators from Resurrection Primary School, Popondetta Primary School and Sorovi Primary School for their tireless commitment over the last four days.

The closing program included speeches from the BOM Chairman, external invigilators, teachers and parents, followed by a token of appreciation (Bondo) from the Grade 8 parents.

item.title: K12.5 million for El Nino relief in WHP
item.description: Western Highlands Province has received K12.5 million from the National Government for El Nino preparedness and response, but Provincial Administrator Joseph Iri Mangbil says the funding falls short of what the province needs to protect its people from the prolonged disaster. Mr. Mangbil says the Western Highlands Provincial Administration initially submitted a funding request of K21.7 million to
item.content:encoded:
Western Highlands Province has received K12.5 million from the National Government for El Nino preparedness and response, but Provincial Administrator Joseph Iri Mangbil says the funding falls short of what the province needs to protect its people from the prolonged disaster.

Mr. Mangbil says the Western Highlands Provincial Administration initially submitted a funding request of K21.7 million to the responsible national government department following an assessment of the province's needs.

However, only K12.5 million was approved, leaving the province to manage the El Nino situation with significantly less than it had requested.

The funding has been allocated to the four districts, with each receiving K2.5 million to implement their respective preparedness and response plans.

Mangbil adds Western Highlands faces a major challenge because of its population of about 700,000 people, which continues to grow as people migrate into the province from other parts of the Highlands.

He also adds the growing population will place additional pressure on available resources as authorities work to respond to the effects of El Nino.

“With our population of about 700,000 people, including those coming into the province from other Highlands provinces, responding to this El Nino situation will be a major challenge.”

Despite the funding shortfall, Mangbil stress public servants must not become complacent but should step up their efforts to ensure assistance reaches the people who need it.

He has reminded officers at all levels of government to remain committed to their duties and carry out their responsibilities effectively during this period of national disaster.

The Western Highlands Provincial Government will also contribute K500,000 to support district-level preparedness and response activities, in addition to the national funding.

The contribution from the provincial government is expected to be shared among the four districts, although the exact allocation to each district has yet to be confirmed.

The Chair of the Provincial Disaster Committee has also urged public servants to exercise patience, fairness and impartiality when dealing with communities affected by the disaster.

He says the effects of El Nino can create anxiety among the people, making it important for government officers to respond wisely and professionally, even when they face difficult situations.

He emphasises on cooperation, responsible leadership and proper management of available funds will be critical to helping Western Highlands communities cope with the prolonged El Nino conditions.

item.title: AI linear accelerator for POM Gen cancer patients
item.description: Cancer patients will soon receive pin-point precision treatment with Papua New Guinea's first AI-powered Linear Accelerator installed at the Port Moresby General Hospital Comprehensive Cancer Center. The Elekta Linear Accelerator from the United States is housed inside Bunker One, a full concrete structure with walls about 1.5 meters thick designed to safely contain radiation.
item.content:encoded:
Cancer patients will soon receive pin-point precision treatment with Papua New Guinea's first AI-powered Linear Accelerator installed at the Port Moresby General Hospital Comprehensive Cancer Center.

The Elekta Linear Accelerator from the United States is housed inside Bunker One, a full concrete structure with walls about 1.5 meters thick designed to safely contain radiation.

Chief Executive Officer of PomGen, Dr. Paki Molumi, said this is the first of its kind in the country, and a major upgrade from the old cobalt source machine in Lae.

"Radiotherapy machine, it's a linear accelerator from Elekta. Compare this to the one in Lae, it's a cobalt source. The thing about radiotherapy machines, if it's cobalt, it's going to burn your skin. It will burn your muscles all the way to get into the target.

Whereas this latest machine, it subtracts everything and only targets the cancer. Precisely, to the point of a pin. We are so lucky we are building this at a time of the AI age. Machines now have inbuilt AI to assist technicians," Dr. Molumi said.

Unlike the cobalt source which releases continuous radiation, the linear accelerator generates radiation on demand by electricity when patients are being treated.

Bunker Two will house a bigger TrueBeam machine, another version of Elekta to complement the first machine and treat different types of cancers depending on depth – neck, abdomen and other deep-seated organs.

According to Dr. Molumi, the radiation oncologist will decide which bunker a patient goes to, adding that the second machine is yet to be procured, with funding hoped for in the 2027 Budget.

For safety, bunkers are fitted with laser beams that pick-up movement and automatically shut down the machine if someone enters during radiation. Operators monitor patients from a shielded monitoring station with computers and cameras.

To make patients feel at home, Dr. Molumi said sterile walls will be covered with murals with PNG cultural designs.

He explained that the treatment workflow is linked, cancer is mapped out and programmed in the Planning CT room, and that information is fed into the linear accelerator to apply treatment directly to the planned field.

After treatment, response will be monitored in nuclear medicine through (Positron Emission Tomography) or PET Scan and Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT or CT) machines.

A SPECT/CT machine is a hybrid imaging system that combines SPECT with X‑ray Computed Tomography (CT) to provide both functional and anatomical imaging in a single scan.

Patients are injected with radioactive material with a half-life of 3-4 hours and kept in uptake rooms before scanning. The scan shows at cellular level whether chemotherapy or radiotherapy is curing the patient.

"After treatment is done, we will need to monitor at molecular level, because you don't know whether your radiotherapy or chemotherapy is actually curing this patient. That's where you get a PET scan. You can actually see the function at cellular level, whether treatment is responding.

Then you can increase dose, reduce dose, or look for other ways," Dr. Molumi explained.

The facility will be able to treat 30 to 60 patients per day when both machines are running.

item.title: WHP priorities water and food
item.description: Western Highlands Province is prioritising access to clean drinking water and food supplies as the effects of El Nino continue to threaten communities in the province.
